title: Setting up a self-hosted Github Action Runner on Azure
content:
This page is for internal DevOps team. This page contains a step through of how to set up a working runner for Github Actions in Azure, but does not necessarily conform to best practices yet.

Setting up the runner

Resources in Azure

You can either set it all up through the UI, or ideally using an Infrastructure-as-Code tool such as Terraform to ensure reproducibility and documentation. If you go through the UI, you will need to set up a Load Balancer and a Virtual Machine and connect them to each other. If you use an IaC tool you will have to define all the resources required.

The following resources are in place when done:

  • 1 Load Balancer

  • 1 Virtual Machine

  • 1 Virtual Network

  • 1 Network Interface

  • 1 Network security group

  • 1 Public IP adress

  • 1 SSH key

  • 1 SSD disk

Load Balancer settings

Create a Backend Pool and attach the VM to that pool. Attach the public IP to the load balancer. This is done under the Frontend IP Configuration blade. Inbound NAT rules sets up access to your VM. For our use case we only allow SSH in. For Outbound rules we allow all traffic out currently. This is something that can and should be limited moving forward.

Virtual Machine settings

VM Size: Standard D2s v3 (2 vcpus, 8 GiB memory)

OS: Ubuntu 20.04

Installing the runner and connecting it to your repository

For a full detailed guide, see Githubs Documentation.

Before moving ahead, ensure you have SSH access to your VM

In our use case we want to connect the runner to only one repository and not the entire organisation. Go to your repository settings on Github. Under the Actions menu on the left hand side there is a sub-menu called Runners, go there. On this page click the button New self-hosted runner.

On the following page choose the correct architecture, in our case Linux and x64. When you do that, the remaining steps will be outlined below on the page. It’s a very simple task from there. It’s a sequence of running a few commands on the VM.

  • Create a folder

  • Download the binary

  • Config the runner

    • During configuration make sure to tag the runner if it has any special dependencies installed, for example PHP or something.

  • Install it as a service

Updating the runner and installing core depencies

The VM needs to updated and Docker is required to be able to run workflows. Additionally we also require the Azure CLI since we are fetching secrets from the Azure Key Vault.

Updating Ubuntu:

sudo apt-get upgrade

Improvements

When time allows and/or needs arise the following improvements should be made

  • Create a reusable Terraform Module to share with IPEX

  • Ensure best practices are followed when setting the worker up in regards to security and and sustainability

  • Set up proper scheduling so that the worker is not always on
